messages:
lina: Quick sync — I ran fused-Flash vs paged-attn microbenchmarks with interleaved KV and a separate-KV layout on A100. Seeing a hard cliff at seq_len=2048 for fused on interleaved, ~18% slower than separate. Need to pick kernel selection + default KV layout for 2.0 runtime.

ryan: can you paste the numbers? :thinking:

lina: pasted raw numbers below (ms per token, median of 10):
```
model: 7B
batch=1
seq_len 256: fused=1.8, paged=2.1
seq_len 512: fused=2.2, paged=2.6
seq_len 1024: fused=3.5, paged=3.8
seq_len 2048: fused=5.7, paged=4.8  <-- regression on fused (interleaved)
```
Note: with separate-KV layout fused=4.1 at 2048.

kevin: interesting. what dtype were the KV tensors? fp16? bf16? any quant?

lina: fp16 for all runs. I also tried bf16, same pattern but slightly higher mem usage. int8-quant (per-channel) reduces mem but introduces >5% quality drift, so not default.

maria: did you profile memory access patterns? sounds like a coalescing / stride issue.

lina: yes — used nvprof / Nsight. Paged-attn has fewer scattered loads because it keeps page-aligned blocks; fused uses a continuous interleaved layout but our allocator gave 256B misalignment for some KV buffers causing uncoalesced L2 loads at big strides.

perf-bot: benchmark summary uploaded: https://perf.internal/redwood/attn/kernbench/1768897777

ryan: so two levers: (A) change allocator/alignment to 4096B for KV pages so interleaved stays coalesced, (B) prefer separate-KV layout for long sequences and route to paged-attn. Which is lower-risk?

kevin: allocator fix is low risk if we can force posix_memalign / CUB allocator tweak. But may increase overall memory consumption slightly (padding). Separate-KV layout increases code complexity (index mapping + extra memcpy on KV restore) but gives stable perf for fused at high seq.

lina: agree. patch I prototyped: posix_memalign(&ptr, 4096, bytes) + ensure stride % 128 == 0 for GPU loads. Quick snippet: 
```
// ensure 128B alignment for KV rows
void* raw = nullptr;
posix_memalign(&raw, 4096, total_bytes);
kv_ptr = reinterpret_cast<float*>(raw);
// stride bytes = round_up(cols * sizeof(float), 128)
```
Test run after this shows fused interleaved at 2048 moves from 5.7 -> 4.6 ms/token (close to separate).

maria: nice. any downside? padding increases memory by ~3-6% per KV, might affect peak-capacity packing. Also need to update allocator for Dedicated nodes to keep consistency.

lina: yes. For Dedicated we can expose a config toggle: `kv_alignment_bytes` default 4096 for GPU instance types with >80GB memory, fallback 128 for low-memory. That lets us avoid big waste for tiny instances.

kevin: batching heuristics: if we detect many long-seq requests (>1024) in the window, we should route to paged-attn and separate-KV to keep latency stable. If mostly short (<512), prefer fused interleaved. Can we implement a cheap sampler in the scheduler?

ryan: scheduler already tracks seq_len histogram per route. Add rule: if p(seq_len>1024) > 0.2 over last 30s then prefer paged/split layout for new workers. We'll need to warm cache for existing workers.

lina: also saw a regression introduced by commit 0a3f9c — changed default stride calc to `cols * sizeof(float)` without rounding. That explains misaligned pages. I have a draft revert and an added test to assert alignment % 128 == 0 for all KV allocations.

maria: add unit that allocates wide KV with random sizes + validates coalesced load heuristic in CI. If we catch misalignment before rollout we avoid perf cliffs.

infra-bot: deploy plan suggested:
- canary allocator fix to 10% of traffic on staging cluster
- run perf gate: median token ms per seq_len at 2048 must be <= previous baseline + 5%
- if pass, rollout to dedicated + hosted next week

kevin: one more thing — fused-Flash kernels assume contiguous K,V with stride matching 128B. For mixed-dtype models (some layers bf16), we need to unify KV dtype at kernel interface to avoid extra transposes. That might buy 1-2% more perf. Suggest we cast to fp16 at allocation time for runtime (configurable).

lina: good call. I can add a `kv_dtype_override` option. Defaults: inherit model dtype, but for inference server we may override to fp16 for fastest kernel path. We'll measure quality impact.

ryan: action items: 
- lina: push allocator alignment fix PR + CI alignment test (ETA: today)
- lina/kevin: prototype scheduler rule and config knobs for kv_alignment_bytes and kv_dtype_override (ETA: EOD Fri)
- maria: add perf CI test for seq_len 2048 baseline (ETA: Tue)
- infra-bot: run canary once PR merged

lina: cool. I'll attach the NVTX flame screenshot and the raw Nsight capture to the perf ticket. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kevin: looks solid. ping me if the canary shows any memory OOMs.

ryan: thanks — if allocator fix solves it, we can keep interleaved as default and avoid separate-KV complexity. If not, we fallback to routing to paged-attn for long sequences.

perf-bot: noted actions: create perf-ticket #PR-4802, expected regression window monitoring enabled.
